observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. South: a squat, splay-legged olive reptile seen head-on, with a large rounded, ribbed brown-and-olive sail spread out behind it as a wide semicircular fan. East: a full side profile of a low quadruped with a tall rounded dorsal sail along most of the back, a long narrow gharial-like snout, webbed feet and a thick tapering tail. North: the rear view of the body and tail pointing toward the camera, with the sail seen edge-on as a thin vertical ridged blade. All three are the same height.
observed.south.png: Front view. The face points at the camera: two eyes, a short snout with small teeth, and the chest. The forelegs are splayed with webbed feet, and the hind feet show behind. The sail rises behind the head as a broad fan shaped like a wheel or peacock tail, with radiating spines, a dark rust edge and olive-mottled bands. The skin is olive with dark mottling. Clean alpha.
observed.east.png: Side profile facing right. A low-slung body on four short, bent legs with webbed toes and a thick tail tapering to the left. The tall rounded sail spans from the shoulders to the base of the tail. It is the tallest element, rust-brown at the scalloped top edge and olive-banded lower down. The snout is long and very narrow, like a gharial, with a row of small teeth along the jaw. The body is olive with dark spots and the belly paler. Painterly and realistic. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Rear view. The tail points toward the viewer at the bottom centre and the hind legs splay out with webbed feet. The back is seen at an angle, with no face or eyes. The sail shows edge-on as a narrow vertical ridged crest, rust at the top, rising above the shoulders. The body reads a little narrow and spindly compared with the bulky south view. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the animal is about 3.5 cells long, much larger than the human and roughly 1.5 to 2 times their height to the top of the sail. At 32 px per cell the sail and long body still read clearly as a sail-backed reptile against the ground.

edits.change: The head has a broad, heavy predator jaw. Two long lower fangs rise past the upper lip and stay visible in side and front views. The snout is still long and sensitive, with a thick base, a wide mouth and a blunt tip carrying sensory pits.

The dorsal fan-spine is one tall, thin, longitudinal sail running along the centreline of the back, from the shoulders to the hips. In the east (side) view it shows its full tall profile. In the south (front) and north (rear) views it is seen nearly edge-on, a narrow upright blade rising from the middle of the back, with the same thin width in both views.

In the front view the broad jaw spans most of the head width, and the two lower fangs show clearly as pale curved points on either side of the upper lip. In the side view they show as pale curved points rising past the upper lip. Teeth along the jaw are few and large, not small and even.

Keep the body, palette and skin colouring of the previous render: a sleek, swamp-built amphibian body with a long sensitive snout. Head: a broad, heavy predator jaw on a long, thick-based snout with a blunt, sensory-pitted tip. Two long pale lower fangs rise past the upper lip and stay clearly visible in front and side views, and the teeth are few and large. Dorsal spine: one tall, thin, longitudinal sail along the centreline of the back, from shoulders to hips, as the creature's one large spine. Side view (east): the sail shows its full tall profile above the back, the broad jaw shows in profile, and the lower fangs rise past the upper lip. Front view (south): the sail is seen nearly edge-on as a narrow upright blade rising from the middle of the back behind the head, the broad jaw spans the head width, and both lower fangs show. Rear view (north): the back, tail and haunches show, the eyes are hidden, and the sail is the same narrow edge-on blade as in the front view. Realistic painterly vanilla RimWorld sprite style, soft painted edges in a deeper shade of the local colour, clean dark outline. Exactly ONE creature, centred, the whole body visible with nothing cut off. Fully transparent background with no ground, no water, no shadow, no text and no border.
